title: Singular owner forms: minun, sinun, hänen
summary: Use minun, sinun, hänen before a supplied possessed noun.
objectives: Use minun, sinun, hänen before a supplied possessed noun.
Apply this rule with the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: This pack groups one owner, not the number of owned things. minun means “my”, sinun means “your” (one person), and hänen means “his” or “her”; Finnish does not distinguish gender here.

An owner form says whose thing something is. Put it before the possessed noun. The noun forms and Tämä on (“This is”) in these examples are supplied; you will learn the endings and sentence construction separately.
minä (“I”) becomes minun (“my”); sinä (“you”) becomes sinun (“your”); hän (“he/she”) becomes hänen (“his/her”).
This owner group can own one thing or several things. The later lessons teach both object numbers.
keyPoints: Use minun, sinun, hänen before a supplied possessed noun.

steps: Tämä on (“This is”) and the complete noun form are supplied.
Use minun (“my”) before the noun; its basic personal form is minä.
Tämä on (“This is”) and the complete noun form are supplied.
Use sinun (“your”) before the noun; its basic personal form is sinä.
Tämä on (“This is”) and the complete noun form are supplied.
Use hänen (“his”) before the noun; its basic personal form is hän.

commonMistakes: Do not use minä, sinä, hän where an owner form is needed.
Use the supplied noun form; suffix formation is taught separately.
